subject: Post-call follow-up: scale-up choreography & prewarmed-slot allocation
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Vargas <elena.vargas@fintechco.com>, FintechCo SRE <sre@fintechco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call follow-up: scale-up choreography & prewarmed-slot allocation

Hi Elena / Fintech SRE team —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + concrete next steps so we have a single source of truth:

High-level SLO targets you asked us to validate:
- P95 latency (streaming responses): <= 150 ms for first byte under nominal payloads (avg prompt ~120 tokens)
- Sustained throughput target: 200 concurrent streaming sessions per region
- Burst capability: handle up to 1,000 concurrent requests for short spikes (<= 90s) with graceful degradation thereafter
- Scale-up latency: aim for warm-slot activation within 20s for reserved warm pool slots; fallback queueing window 30–45s

Design notes / assumptions from the call:
- We recommend a hybrid approach: maintain a small warm pool (N prewarmed slots) plus a fast spin-up path that uses pre-initialized container images and KV cache priming.
- For cost reasons we suggested 25–40 prewarmed slots in primary region as a starting point (we agreed to simulation to refine).
- If warm pool exhausted, requests enter a short FIFO queue with backpressure signals; after 45s requests fall back to a lower-cost model variant (smaller context / quantized) to preserve throughput.

Action items (owners + suggested due dates):
1) Redwood simulation plan: Aditya to produce a parametric load test (spike shape + prompt distribution) and a recommended warm pool sizing table — due 2028-06-03. Attachment: priming_latency_matrix.csv (initial latency numbers by model variant).
2) Warm pool design doc: Marissa to share trimmed design + cost delta (on/off) and options for pre-KV priming — due 2028-06-05. Attachment: warm_pool_design.pdf.
3) Runbook snippet: Sean to draft queueing/backpressure window and alert thresholds (p95 > 200ms, queue length > 150) — due 2028-06-02.
4) FintechCo: please confirm your peak burst window expectations (duration, expected concurrent QPS) and any regulatory constraints on prewarmed capacity by 2028-06-01.

Open questions for the simulation we flagged on the call:
- Typical prompt length distribution (we asked for 90/10 split short/long)
- Acceptable fallbacks (is switching model quantization acceptable for overflow?)
- Cost cap per hour for warm pool at 80% utilization

I attached the initial latency matrix (priming_latency_matrix.csv) and the warm pool sketch (warm_pool_design.pdf). We’ll iterate after Aditya’s sims land.

Thanks — Kim
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

---

Date: 2028-05-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call follow-up: scale-up choreography & prewarmed-slot allocation

Kim / team —

Thanks for the concise recap. A few clarifications from our side before you run sims:
1) Peak burst expectations: we see short bursts of up to ~1,200 concurrent API sessions but typically only for 30–60s tied to batch payroll events. Longer sustained loads (5–10 min) are rarer but possible during third-party vendor outages.
2) Fallback model: switching to a smaller quantized model is acceptable for non-critical paths, but our fraud detection flows must stay on the higher-fidelity model (no quantization allowed). We’ll provide a list of endpoint tags that must never fallback.
3) Cost cap: we want an estimate, but ballpark hourly cap for warm pool cost is $1,200/hr in primary region — we’ll validate with finance.

Lastly, can you note how token-level streaming (early tokens on response) behaves during queueing? We need to understand partial-response guarantees.

Elena
Elena Vargas
Director, Platform Engineering — FintechCo
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Elena Vargas <elena.vargas@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-30T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call follow-up: scale-up choreography & prewarmed-slot allocation

Elena —

Short answers to your items and notes we’ll fold into the simulation:
- 1,200 concurrent short spikes: we’ll run a 90s step with linear ramp to 1,200 and observe p50/p95/p99 for first byte and tail.
- Partial-response during queueing: streaming begins only once a streaming session is assigned a warmed or spun-up slot. If the request sits in queue beyond your tolerance, we can return a 102 Processing + estimated wait and optionally stream partial placeholders, but we do not stream actual model tokens until the KV/cache is available for that session.
- For fraud detection endpoints (no-fallback list): mark these as high-priority routing — they will get prewarmed slots first and will never be routed to quantized fallback. Please send the list by 2028-06-01.

Technical notes for the simulation and priming behavior (for Marissa / Sean to incorporate):
- KV priming: we’ll simulate cold vs primed KV cache influence; expect an extra 80–140 ms on p95 when KV cache is cold for long-context prompts.
- Warm pool activation: measured cold-start (container boot + model init) = ~12–18s on our optimized path; plus KV priming 8–12s. That’s why prewarmed slots cut activation to < 20s.
- Queue policy: suggest strict FIFO for identical priority classes; promote high-priority endpoints when warm pool frees.

I’ll deliver the test harness and initial results by EOD 2028-06-03 to the shared drive link.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call follow-up: scale-up choreography & prewarmed-slot allocation

Elena —

Appreciate the prompt reply and the burst characteristics — that’s exactly what we needed. Quick closing notes and timeline:
- Aditya: run the 90s ramp to 1,200 and a 45s spike at 1,000; include p50/p95/p99 and cold/primed KV splits — deliver to shared drive by 2028-06-03 EOD.
- Marissa: cost delta + 3 sizing options (conservative, balanced, aggressive) for prewarmed slots — 2028-06-05.
- Sean: playbook draft for queue thresholds and alerts — 2028-06-02.
- FintechCo: send the no-fallback endpoint list and confirm cost cap by 2028-06-01.

We’ll schedule a review session the week of 2028-06-06 to go over results and pick an initial configuration for a 4-week pilot. I’ll send a calendar invite once Aditya has the initial results.

Thanks all — looking forward to the sims.

Kim
